layaR

Source: CLAUDE.md

An R package that runs Laya System 1 decision models locally: typed choice, score and yes/no questions with calibrated probabilities. R talks to the laya-onnx Rust crate through extendr, and laya-onnx runs the models with ONNX Runtime (ORT). No Python is needed at prediction time.

  • Repo: https://github.com/gueyenono/layaR (public). Site: https://gueyenono.github.io/layaR/
  • Upstream: https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya (the laya-rust/ folder is laya-onnx).
  • Design history, decisions and roadmap: plan/layaR.md (long; read the section you need). Upstream asks and their status: plan/upstream-issues.md.
  • Notes about the maintainer’s own machine (paths, Nix setup) are in CLAUDE.local.md, which is not committed.

State (2026-11-22)

  • Latest release: v0.2.0 (2026-11-21). main is at 0.2.0.9000 (development). Since the release, main gained only tests and docs: the typed-decisions parity fixture (PR #16), vignettes re-knitted with 0.2.0 plus advice on threads (PR #17), and these notes (PRs #14, #15). NEWS.md’s development section is still empty.

  • 0.2.0 switched to loading ORT at run time (load-dynamic, PR #12). Before that, ORT was linked statically and downloaded during the build, which broke Windows and Intel Macs.

  • Platforms:

    Platform Status
    Linux x86_64 Supported. CI, plus full parity (LAYAR_PARITY=all) run locally for all three checkpoints.
    macOS arm64 Supported. CI, plus model tests and parity for all three checkpoints via model-tests.yaml.
    Windows x64 Supported since 0.2.0. CI, plus model tests and parity for all three checkpoints via model-tests.yaml.
    Linux arm64 Should work (the ORT download covers it), but untested.
    Intel Mac Builds, but Microsoft publishes no ORT for it; predictions need a user-supplied ORT >= 1.27.
    Windows arm64, wasm Not supported.

  • r-universe: builds only GitHub releases (registry gueyenono/gueyenono.r-universe.dev, "branch": "*release"), not main; it picks up a release in about an hour. 0.2.0 built (2026-11-21) for Linux, macOS (arm64 and x86_64) and Windows (x86_64 and arm64); only wasm fails. Windows arm64 and Intel Mac binaries build, but have no ORT download. A Linux install from r-universe was verified; Windows and macOS installs from r-universe are not yet. Status: https://gueyenono.r-universe.dev/api/packages/layaR

  • Open items:

    • Install the 0.2.0 binary from r-universe on Windows and macOS (needs a real machine).
    • Linux arm64 is untested.
    • Ask upstream to move laya-onnx to ort rc.15+ (fixes the failed-load bug below); not filed.
    • CRAN (next item).

  • CRAN: not submitted. The blocker (ORT downloaded at build time) is gone. What’s left is plan §9.4 “Other CRAN checklist items” and Phase 7: vendoring (rextendr::vendor_pkgs()), tarball size, cran-comments.md, and win-builder/rhub checks.

Layout

  • R/: the user API. The main files:
    • engine.R: engines, the default engine, connect().
    • predict.R, questions.R, presets.R, results.R, annotate.R (data frames), text.R.
    • models.R: model root, Hugging Face download, laya_import_model().
    • runtime.R: ORT lookup, download and load.
    • json.R: all R↔︎JSON conversion. Always use to_json(), with digits = NA.
    • conditions.R: laya_abort() and the error kinds.
  • R/extendr-wrappers.R: generated. Every build regenerates it (the document binary in src/rust/document.rs). Never edit it by hand.
  • src/rust/: the bridge crate laya_r. It is thin: JSON in, JSON out, no inference logic.
    • Every rs_* function returns an envelope (envelope.rs). R unwraps it with rs_unwrap() and raises laya_error_<kind> conditions.
    • runtime.rs loads ORT.
    • questions.rs and results.rs translate the Python formats.
  • src/Makevars.in and tools/config.R: from rextendr’s templates. configure runs tools/config.R.
  • tests/testthat/: model-free tests run everywhere; model-backed tests skip without a model.
    • helper-runtime.R provides skip_without_runtime().
    • fixtures/parity/{multilingual,english,typed-decisions}.json are generated by data-raw/make_fixtures.R.
  • vignettes/*.Rmd are precomputed: edit the .Rmd.orig files, then knit them (see “Docs”).
  • laya-repo/: a local clone of upstream laya (https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya), ignored by git and by R CMD build. Its golden tests (laya-rust/tests/golden/) are the fixture source; clone it there to regenerate fixtures. The current fixtures came from commit 80a1da1 (0.4.34), older than the pinned v0.5.1, which made no API changes.
  • data-raw/: dev scripts.
    • make_fixtures.R: builds the parity and text fixtures.
    • knit_vignettes.R: knits the vignettes.
    • parity_sweep.R: an old manual parity script.

Build and test

  • Since 0.2.0, building needs only Rust (rustc >= 1.85): no OpenSSL and no network beyond fetching crates.
  • Install: R CMD INSTALL .. The release build with LTO takes a few minutes; src/rust/target is git-ignored and can grow to several GB.
  • Docs and NAMESPACE: Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'.
  • Tests: Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'. With a model installed, set NOT_CRAN=true so parity runs.
    • LAYAR_PARITY=all runs all 117 parity cases per checkpoint (about 6 minutes each).
    • LAYAR_TEST_RUNTIME=true makes the tests download ORT when it’s missing, and fail rather than skip if it won’t load.
  • By default models live in tools::R_user_dir("layaR","cache")/onnx/<checkpoint> (see laya_model_root()) and ORT in tools::R_user_dir("layaR","data")/onnxruntime/<version>/.
  • test-bridge.R’s model_dir() hard-codes R_user_dir("layaR","cache")/onnx/multilingual. It ignores layaR.model_root.
  • Check: Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'. Site: pkgdown::check_pkgdown() and pkgdown::build_site().

ONNX Runtime (R/runtime.R, src/rust/src/runtime.rs)

  • Lookup order:
    1. options(layaR.onnxruntime = path).
    2. The ORT_DYLIB_PATH environment variable.
    3. layaR’s own install: tools::R_user_dir("layaR","data")/onnxruntime/1.28.0/<lib>.
  • Download: laya_install_runtime() downloads the NuGet package Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime 1.28.0 (139 MB), checks the SHA-512 that NuGet publishes, and extracts this platform’s library.
    • microsoft/onnxruntime GitHub releases returned 404 from here, so NuGet is the source.
    • options(layaR.onnxruntime_url=) overrides the URL (the tests use it).
  • When it runs:
    • laya_download_model() installs the runtime if it’s missing.
    • connect() calls ensure_runtime() before the first engine. Interactive sessions get a prompt; others get laya_error_runtime_not_found.
  • Pins that must move together:
    • the ort crate version (=2.0.0-rc.13, default-features = false, features = ['load-dynamic']) in src/rust/Cargo.toml;
    • ort_version, ort_min_version, ort_nupkg_sha512 and ort_nupkg_size_mb in R/runtime.R;
    • ORT_VERSION in lib.rs.
    rc.13 with api-27 requires ORT >= 1.27. Newer ORT versions load fine; older ones are refused.
  • One load per process: ORT loads once per R session and can’t be swapped; restart R to change it.
  • ort rc.13 bug: a failed load permanently breaks later loads in that process (uninitialized OnceLock). runtime.rs therefore checks the library itself first (opens, OrtGetApiBase, version) and sets POISONED if ort still fails. ort rc.15 fixed this (commit 0381990), but laya v0.5.1 uses rc.13. If laya moves to rc.15+, the pre-check can stay but the comment should be updated.
  • Threads: with Microsoft’s ORT build, more intra-op threads than physical cores is slow. On a 4-core/8-thread i7-4790K (2026-11-22), 0.2.0 and 0.1.1 (ORT linked in) took the same time at 2 and 4 threads and at the default (one per physical core). At 8 threads 0.2.0 was about 45% slower (about 900 ms against 600 ms for the triage preset). The default never goes past the physical cores. The vignette advises against more, and notes that parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE) doesn’t count physical cores on Linux.
  • Windows: onnxruntime.dll needs the MSVC runtime (vcruntime140/msvcp140). The runtime_load error mentions the Visual C++ Redistributable.

Upstream pins

  • laya-onnx is pinned to tag v0.5.1 (commit 090c540), with default-features = false and features = ['load-dynamic'].
    • Its download feature stays off: models are downloaded from R.
    • Keep LAYA_ONNX_REV in src/rust/src/lib.rs in sync.
  • Upgrading:
    1. Bump the tag.
    2. Run cargo update -p laya-onnx.
    3. Run full parity locally.
    4. Run model-tests.yaml on Windows and macOS.
  • Upstream asks (plan/upstream-issues.md):
    • U1, publish ONNX exports on Hugging Face (laya#1504): still open. layaR downloads from its own re-host instead: https://huggingface.co/gueyenono/laya-onnx (unchanged Apache-2.0 weights).
    • U2, load-dynamic (laya#1505): done.
    • U3–U5: not filed.

CI (.github/workflows)

  • R-CMD-check.yaml: runs on push and PR.
    • Matrix: macOS arm64, Windows, and Ubuntu (release, devel, oldrel-1).
    • It downloads and caches ORT and sets LAYAR_TEST_RUNTIME=true. There’s no model, so the model tests skip (about 17 skips).
    • Windows needs the x86_64-pc-windows-gnu Rust target. The runner context isn’t available in job-level env, hence the GITHUB_ENV step. actions/cache rejects paths containing ...
  • model-tests.yaml: manual. It also runs on PRs that change the workflow file.
    • Start it with gh workflow run model-tests.yaml --ref <branch> -f os=windows-latest|macos-latest|ubuntu-latest|all -f checkpoint=multilingual|english|typed-decisions|all -f parity=core|all.
    • Models (0.8–1 GB each) and ORT are cached per OS. GitHub caches are branch-scoped: a branch can restore its own caches and those made on main, nothing else. Every model cache so far was made on a feature branch that is now deleted (load-dynamic-runtime, parity-typed-decisions), so the next run on a new branch downloads the models again. Running the workflow once on main makes caches every branch can use.
    • The repo’s caches total about 10.7 GB (2026-11-22), over GitHub’s 10 GB limit, so GitHub is evicting the least recently used ones. Deleting the stale model caches would free about 8 GB: gh cache list, gh cache delete <id>.
    • Last runs: 2026-11-21, all green on Windows and macOS for every checkpoint (core parity); 2026-11-22, typed-decisions with all parity cases on both, green.
  • pkgdown.yaml: builds the site; deploys on main and on releases.

Test coverage gaps

  • Bridge, predict, annotate and robustness tests use multilingual only.
  • Windows rejects laya_import_model(method = "symlink"): symlink detection fails there, so the default there is "copy".

Docs

  • README.Rmd → README.md: devtools::build_readme(). It needs a model.
  • Vignettes: edit vignettes/*.Rmd.orig (and vignettes/articles/*.Rmd.orig), then run Rscript data-raw/knit_vignettes.R [name ...] after installing the current layaR. This needs models and takes a while for the benchmarks.
    • All vignettes were last knitted on 2026-11-22 with layaR 0.2.0 (PR #17).
    • Knit the benchmarks (models-and-performance) on an idle machine: closing a browser or chat app isn’t enough if it keeps running in the background. Benchmark tables are noisy; check that the prose still matches the numbers after each knit.
    • Prose-only fixes can be made in both the .orig and the knitted .Rmd without knitting again.
  • Add each new exported function to _pkgdown.yml’s reference index.
  • After any dependency change, regenerate LICENSE.note with rextendr::write_license_note(). Then re-add the hand-written tail: ORT is not included, and the test fixtures are Apache-2.0 from Convai Innovations.

Releasing (the pattern used for 0.1.1 and 0.2.0)

  1. Merge feature PRs into main with merge commits (gh pr merge N --merge).
  2. Open a branch release-X.Y.Z and a PR “Release X.Y.Z”. It only changes Version: in DESCRIPTION and renames the # layaR (development version) heading in NEWS.md. Merge it once CI is green.
  3. Publish the release on that merge commit: gh release create vX.Y.Z --target <sha> --title "layaR X.Y.Z" --notes-file <that NEWS section>. r-universe picks it up within about an hour.
  4. Later, a PR “Start development version X.Y.Z.9000” bumps DESCRIPTION and adds a new # layaR (development version) heading.

Conventions

  • Commit or push only when asked. Work on a branch and open a PR; don’t push to main.
  • End commit messages with Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. End PR bodies with 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).
  • Errors: use laya_abort(msg, kind = ...). Every failure is a classed laya_error_<kind>. Document new kinds in R/conditions.R, and test them with expect_error(..., class = "laya_error_<kind>").
  • Options are documented in R/layaR-package.R: layaR.checkpoint, layaR.threads, layaR.model_root, layaR.model_repo, layaR.onnxruntime, layaR.shared_cache.
  • Each engine holds about 1–1.6 GB. Tests keep one engine alive at a time.
  • Add user-visible changes to NEWS.md under the development heading.
